title: Wald test as a named estimate-over-SE test
dek: Wikipedia Wald: (θ̂−θ0)/SE. Easy, and fragile under transformation and separation. Complementary to stats-wald-score.
story: The Wald test on Wikipedia is the celebrity intern test: take the MLE, divide by a standard error, refer to Normal or χ². It only needs the full model.

It is not invariant to reparameterisation in finite samples (delta-method cousins). It explodes when SEs are nonsense (complete separation in logit). stats-wald-score already said so; this is the encyclopedia name.
Reporting 'Wald p' from a sandwich SE is a different costume than using Fisher information — say which curvature you used.
deep: Near a boundary, Wald's quadratic approximation of ℓ is a lie.
Profile CIs and LRTs are often more trustworthy for nonlinear parameters (transmission probabilities, ICs50).
stats-delta-method is how Wald on g(θ) is built.
Do not treat a huge Wald z on a Firth-needed logit as a discovery.

visual.caption: Wald pretends the MLE is Normal with variance from curvature. Separation/skew makes that cartoon fail while a score/LRT may still be finite.
